items.heading: Indian courtyard houses (Angan)
details: An open central courtyard can improve ventilation, daylight, and thermal regulation through the home.

items.heading: Verandah / Otla / Arugu / Thinnai
details: A shaded transitional space that reduces direct solar heating on the main walls and welcomes visitors.

items.heading: Jali screens
details: Perforated stone or wood screens allow airflow through a wall while reducing direct sunlight and glare.

items.heading: Deep roof overhangs
details: Reduce solar radiation on walls and protect them from driving rain.

items.heading: Thick masonry walls
details: High thermal mass slows down indoor temperature swings between day and night.

items.heading: High ceilings
details: Allow warm air to rise well above the occupied zone, keeping the living space cooler.

items.heading: Internal courtyards with vegetation
details: Combine shade, greenery, and airflow at the heart of a home.

items.heading: Raised plinths
details: Protect buildings from rainwater, rising moisture, and localized flooding.

items.heading: Terracotta / clay roofing
details: Can moderate heat transfer into the home depending on the construction details.

items.heading: Whitewashed roofs and walls
details: Reflect more solar radiation than dark surfaces, reducing heat gain indoors.

items.heading: Trees around houses
details: Provide shade and additional cooling through evapotranspiration around the building.
